title: GPT-4 lists immune-mediated hemolytic anemia among causes of a Border Collie's worsening anemia; a second vet confirms and treats
summary: GPT-4 listed IMHA among causes of a dog's worsening anemia; a second vet confirmed and treated; the dog recovered, per the owner's thread.
account: A Twitter user, Cooper (@peakcooper), wrote on 25 March 2023 that his Border Collie, Sassy, had been treated for babesiosis but worsened, with pale gums and more severe anemia, while the first vet found no cause and advised waiting. He entered two sets of bloodwork into ChatGPT Plus running GPT-4, which said it was not a veterinarian, then listed possible underlying causes including immune-mediated hemolytic anemia (IMHA). At a second clinic he asked about IMHA; the vet agreed after further tests, treatment began, and Cooper reported an almost full recovery. The New York Post, India Today and Business Insider reported the thread (27 to 30 March); Cooper did not respond to Insider, and no veterinarian has spoken publicly.
purpose: GPT-4, served through ChatGPT, is a general-purpose conversational model built to answer questions and follow instructions; answering a diagnostic question about a dog's bloodwork is an instance of that general use, not a designed veterinary function, and the model itself prefaced its answer by saying it is not a veterinarian.
taxonomy_note: The taxonomy has no diagnostic-support or animal-health type; Knowledge Discovery is used in the narrow sense that the model surfaced a candidate diagnosis the owner then put to a clinician.

ratings.reason: By the owner's own account the diagnosis led to treatment and his dog's near-full recovery; the account is self-reported and unverified by any clinician, and the beneficiary is one owner and one animal.

ai_role.statement: From the owner's typed description and two sets of blood results, GPT-4 explained the trend in the bloodwork and, when asked what else could underlie the anemia, listed candidate causes including IMHA; the owner chose IMHA to put to a second veterinarian, who confirmed it after further tests and treated the dog. Whether that vet would have reached IMHA unprompted is unknown, and the owner himself notes IMHA is a common complication of babesiosis, so the counterfactual is unproven. The owner reported that GPT-3.5 did not reach the diagnosis and said the tool 'should be a tool to be used by professionals'.

produced_by: The owner had two sets of actual blood results plus the babesiosis diagnosis and treatment history, and entered them, with which tests had been run, into GPT-4 via ChatGPT Plus rather than GPT-3.5.
The first vet had no working diagnosis and advised waiting, which left the owner looking for a second opinion.
A second veterinarian was willing to test for the owner-raised hypothesis and confirmed it before treating.
must_hold: A licensed clinician confirms the model's suggestion with tests before any treatment is started.
The model's output is treated as a hypothesis to raise with a clinician, not as a diagnosis, consistent with its own disclaimer.
The underlying data entered are real laboratory results, not a lay description of symptoms alone.

headline: GPT-4 lists IMHA among causes of a dog's anemia; vet confirms

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. Filed as protective response with prevention unproven rather than the classifier's specific harm prevented: every published account traces to the owner's own thread, no vet statement or record has surfaced, Business Insider got no reply from the owner, and the counterfactual is unproven. GPT-4 produced a list of candidate causes that included IMHA, not a single diagnosis. The event is dated to the thread (25 March 2023); the Monitor's ID date (27 March) is the New York Post report.
